key_insight: Repeated droplet impacts can trigger a growing subharmonic Faraday-wave response in a vertically forced bath even when the initially flat bath is linearly stable, by seeding the most susceptible radial mode with finite amplitude.
engineering_relevance: This suggests droplet–surface interactions can unlock unexpected wave growth and mixing in forced liquid systems, which matters for atomization, coating, vibration-driven processing, and wave-controlled fluid devices.
method: Axisymmetric two-phase direct numerical simulations across a wide Reynolds–Weber parameter range
Bath-only simulations with finite-amplitude impact-equivalent perturbations
Floquet analysis and Bessel-mode decomposition to identify the dominant unstable radial mode
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a phenomenological regime map with quasi-periodic, decaying, faint, and unstable-bath regimes, plus agreement between coupled simulations, bath-only perturbation tests, and mode analysis.
watch_item: The mechanism is demonstrated for a finite cylindrical, axisymmetric setup, so transferability to 3D geometries, different bath sizes, or non-ideal droplet impact conditions may require additional validation.
paper_title: Droplet-triggered Faraday waves in a vertically forced bath
